items.q: The gap between gold and silver in the 100 metres was ______ — three hundredths of a second — but in elite sprinting that is the difference between a medal and obscurity.
items.vi: Khoảng cách giữa huy chương vàng và bạc ở cự ly 100 mét là cực kỳ nhỏ — ba phần trăm giây — nhưng trong môn chạy nước rút đỉnh cao, đó là khác biệt giữa một tấm huy chương và sự vô danh.
items.explanation: Word choice: three hundredths of a second is a tiny measurement, so the gap is minute (/maɪˈnjuːt/) = extremely small. ✗ trivial — unimportant, which the sentence denies (it decides a medal); ✗ meagre — too small in quantity to be enough (a meagre salary), not a measured gap; ✗ petty — small-minded, mean behaviour, never a measurement.

items.q: Ever since his boyhood club released him at sixteen, the striker has ______, treating every question about his past as a personal insult.
options: had a chip on his shoulder
had a bee in his bonnet
had a finger in every pie
items.answer: had a chip on his shoulder
items.vi: Kể từ khi câu lạc bộ thời niên thiếu cho anh ra đi năm mười sáu tuổi, tiền đạo này luôn mang nỗi hậm hực trong lòng, coi mọi câu hỏi về quá khứ như một sự xúc phạm cá nhân.
items.explanation: Idiom: treating every question as a personal insult years after being released shows lasting resentment — had a chip on his shoulder = stays bitter about a past injustice and takes offence easily. ✗ had a bee in his bonnet — obsessed with one idea; ✗ had an axe to grind — has a hidden selfish motive; ✗ had a finger in every pie — involved in many activities.

items.q: After nine hours of deliberation, the jury in the data-fraud trial ______ a unanimous verdict of guilty on all three counts.
items.vi: Sau chín giờ nghị án, bồi thẩm đoàn trong phiên tòa xét xử vụ gian lận dữ liệu đã đi đến phán quyết nhất trí là có tội ở cả ba tội danh.
items.explanation: Collocation: a jury reaches a verdict — the fixed verb for deciding its answer, and the blank is followed directly by a unanimous verdict with no preposition. ✗ arrived — needs at (arrive at a verdict); ✗ came — needs to (come to a verdict); ✗ achieved — goes with goals, results and success, not verdicts.

items.q: The striker ______ offside when the pass was played; the freeze-frame clearly shows two defenders standing goal-side of him.
items.vi: Tiền đạo không thể nào đã việt vị lúc đường chuyền được thực hiện; hình dừng cho thấy rõ hai hậu vệ đứng gần khung thành hơn anh ta.
items.explanation: Modal deduction about the past: the freeze-frame clearly shows two defenders goal-side, so the speaker is sure offside was impossible — can't have been. ✗ mustn't have been — mustn't is prohibition, not deduction; the negative of must have is can't have; ✗ needn't have been — 'it was unnecessary', not a judgement about a fact; ✗ shouldn't have been — criticises a choice, but being offside is not a decision.

items.q: The world number one ______ the first-round defeat as a blip and was back on the practice court within hours.
items.vi: Tay vợt số một thế giới gạt phăng trận thua vòng một, coi đó chỉ là một sự cố nhỏ, và quay lại sân tập chỉ vài giờ sau.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: as a blip (something unimportant) and back on the practice court within hours show she dismissed the defeat — shrugged off = treated as unimportant. ✗ called off — cancelled (an event); ✗ put off — postponed, or discouraged someone; ✗ fended off — kept away an attacker or awkward questions; a defeat already suffered cannot be fended off.

items.q: Abolishing the offside rule would be a ______ decision, one that historians of the game would still be arguing about a century from now.
items.vi: Bãi bỏ luật việt vị sẽ là một quyết định trọng đại, mà các nhà sử học bóng đá vẫn còn tranh cãi cả trăm năm sau.
items.explanation: Word choice: a decision still argued about a century from now is one of great, lasting importance — momentous. ✗ eminent — distinguished, famous; used of people (an eminent scientist), not decisions; ✗ imposing — impressive in size or appearance, of buildings or figures; ✗ colossal — enormous in physical size or amount (a colossal debt), not in significance.

items.q: Rarely ______ dominated a single Olympic programme so completely, winning all seven of her events by clear water.
items.vi: Hiếm khi có một vận động viên bơi lội nào thống trị trọn vẹn một kỳ Olympic đến thế, thắng cả bảy nội dung với khoảng cách rõ rệt.
items.explanation: Inversion: a negative adverb at the front (Rarely) forces auxiliary + subject, and the past participle dominated needs has: Rarely has a swimmer dominated. ✗ a swimmer has — normal order; no inversion after Rarely; ✗ a swimmer had — no inversion, and past perfect has no earlier point to refer to; ✗ does a swimmer — inverted, but does must be followed by the base form dominate, not dominated.

items.q: The anchor found himself ______ after a live microphone picked him up mocking a guest during the commercial break.
items.vi: Người dẫn chương trình rơi vào rắc rối sau khi micro đang bật thu được cảnh anh ta chế giễu một vị khách trong lúc nghỉ quảng cáo.
items.explanation: Idiom: being picked up mocking a guest on a live microphone lands him in trouble — in hot water = in trouble for something you did. ✗ in the red — owing money, in debt; ✗ in the doldrums — inactive, stagnant or gloomy; ✗ in the dark — not told, uninformed.

items.q: Many freelance reporters, ______ fees have fallen by a third in real terms, can barely make ends ______ on what online outlets pay per article.
items.vi: Nhiều phóng viên tự do, những người có nhuận bút đã giảm một phần ba theo giá trị thực, hầu như không đủ sống với mức các trang tin trực tuyến trả cho mỗi bài.
items.explanation: Double blank: the first gap links reporters to fees as owner and thing owned, so the possessive relative whose (their fees); the second completes the idiom make ends meet = earn just enough to live on. ✗ who / meet — who fees have fallen is ungrammatical: who cannot show possession; ✗ whose / match — match breaks the fixed idiom; ✗ whom / met — whom is an object form, and met is the wrong form in the idiom.

items.q: The public broadcaster's audience has grown steadily over the past two years, ______ its commercial rivals' has shrunk for six quarters in a row.
items.vi: Lượng khán giả của đài truyền hình công đã tăng đều trong hai năm qua, trong khi lượng khán giả của các đối thủ thương mại lại giảm sáu quý liên tiếp.
items.explanation: Linking words: two full clauses with opposite facts (audience has grown … rivals' has shrunk) need a contrast conjunction — whereas. ✗ despite — a preposition, takes a noun or -ing, not subject + verb; ✗ otherwise — an adverb meaning 'if not', and cannot join two clauses with only a comma; ✗ nevertheless — an adverb ('however') that needs a full stop or semicolon before it, not a comma.

items.q: Despite the scale of the doping scandal, the story received only ______ attention from the national broadcasters, which were busy covering the election.
items.vi: Dù vụ bê bối doping có quy mô lớn, câu chuyện chỉ nhận được rất ít sự chú ý từ các đài truyền hình quốc gia, vốn đang bận đưa tin về cuộc bầu cử.
items.explanation: Word choice: only ______ attention = very little attention, and scant is the adjective that pairs with attention/regard. ✗ scarce — in short supply, of resources (water, jobs), not attention; ✗ sparse — thinly spread over an area (sparse hair, a sparse population); ✗ slender — thin in build, or a narrow margin (a slender majority).

items.q: The press ombudsman recommended that the correction ______ on the same page and in the same type size as the original error.
items.vi: Thanh tra báo chí khuyến nghị rằng đính chính phải được đăng trên cùng trang và với cùng cỡ chữ như lỗi ban đầu.
items.explanation: Subjunctive: after recommended that, the that-clause takes the base form, so the passive is be printed. ✗ was printed — past indicative; a recommendation is not a report of what happened; ✗ is printed — present indicative; after recommend/suggest/insist the verb loses its -s and tense; ✗ would be printed — would is not used in a that-clause after recommend.

items.q: Before announcing her candidacy for the federation presidency, she quietly ______ several national coaches to gauge how much support she could count on.
items.vi: Trước khi tuyên bố ứng cử chức chủ tịch liên đoàn, bà đã âm thầm thăm dò ý kiến vài huấn luyện viên đội tuyển quốc gia để xem mình có thể trông cậy vào bao nhiêu sự ủng hộ.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: she quietly approached coaches to gauge support — sounded out = discreetly found out someone's opinion. ✗ spoke out — stated views publicly, and takes no object; ✗ sounded off — complained loudly, no object; ✗ spelled out — explained in detail; you spell out a plan or rules, not people.

items.q: "______," the coach told the gymnast, who was close to tears after her fall; "the all-around final is still two days away."
items.vi: "Cứ ngẩng cao đầu lên," huấn luyện viên nói với cô vận động viên thể dục dụng cụ đang rưng rưng nước mắt sau cú ngã; "chung kết toàn năng vẫn còn hai ngày nữa."
items.explanation: Idiom: the gymnast is close to tears and the coach reminds her the final is still two days away — encouragement: Keep your chin up = stay cheerful and hopeful. ✗ Keep your hair on — calm down, don't get angry; ✗ Keep your shirt on — also 'don't lose your temper'; ✗ Keep your head down — stay quiet and avoid attention.

items.q: The documentary ______ a furious debate about the ethics of secretly filming athletes in their changing rooms.
items.vi: Bộ phim tài liệu đã châm ngòi cho một cuộc tranh luận dữ dội về đạo đức của việc quay lén vận động viên trong phòng thay đồ.
items.explanation: Collocation: causing a discussion to start is spark a debate (also spark controversy / a row), and the verb needs the object a furious debate. ✗ lit — you light a fire or a cigarette, not a debate; ✗ flared — intransitive: a debate flares (up) by itself, it cannot flare something; ✗ blazed — also intransitive (a fire blazes), takes no object.

items.q: The club now regrets ______ the young winger a longer contract before its wealthier rivals came calling.
items.vi: Câu lạc bộ giờ hối tiếc vì đã không đề nghị cầu thủ chạy cánh trẻ một hợp đồng dài hạn hơn trước khi các đối thủ giàu có hơn tìm đến.
items.explanation: Gerund vs infinitive: regret + -ing looks back at something done or not done in the past — the club now regrets not offering the contract before rivals came. ✗ not to offer — regret + to-infinitive only announces bad news now (we regret to inform you); ✗ to not offer — same problem, plus a split infinitive; ✗ not offer — a bare verb cannot follow regret.

items.q: The proposal to expand the tournament to 48 teams was approved by an ______ majority of member associations, with only four voting against.
items.vi: Đề xuất mở rộng giải đấu lên 48 đội đã được đa số áp đảo các liên đoàn thành viên thông qua, chỉ có bốn phiếu chống.
items.explanation: Word choice: approved with only four voting against = a very large majority — overwhelming majority is the fixed pairing. ✗ overriding — more important than everything else (an overriding concern), not 'large'; ✗ overpowering — too strong to resist, of smells or feelings; ✗ overbearing — bossy, domineering, of people.

items.q: The club's spokesman told reporters on Sunday evening that the board ______ the allegations at a press conference the following morning.
items.vi: Người phát ngôn câu lạc bộ nói với các phóng viên tối Chủ nhật rằng ban lãnh đạo sẽ trả lời các cáo buộc tại cuộc họp báo vào sáng hôm sau.
items.explanation: Reported speech: after the past reporting verb told, will backshifts to would, and the following morning shows the event was still future for the speaker. ✗ will address — no backshift after told on a past Sunday; ✗ addresses — present simple reports a general fact, not a planned event; ✗ had addressed — past perfect puts the press conference before Sunday, contradicting the following morning.

items.q: The editor promised to ______ in tracing the source of the leaked memo, even if it meant reviewing every email sent from the building that week.
options: leave a lot to be desired
items.vi: Tổng biên tập hứa sẽ không bỏ sót bất cứ manh mối nào trong việc truy tìm nguồn của bản ghi nhớ bị rò rỉ, kể cả khi phải rà soát mọi email gửi đi từ tòa nhà trong tuần đó.
items.explanation: Idiom: reviewing every email sent from the building means trying every possible way — leave no stone unturned. ✗ leave well alone — not interfere with something that is fine as it is; ✗ leave it at that — say or do nothing more; ✗ leave a lot to be desired — be far from satisfactory.

items.q: ______ how long the power cut would last, the laboratory staff moved the vaccine samples into a backup freezer running on a generator.
items.vi: Không biết sự cố mất điện sẽ kéo dài bao lâu, nhân viên phòng thí nghiệm đã chuyển các mẫu vắc-xin sang tủ đông dự phòng chạy bằng máy phát.
items.explanation: Participle clause: the opening clause gives the reason the staff acted, and the staff are the ones not knowing, so an active -ing form with not in front: Not knowing. ✗ Not known — past participle is passive: the staff were not known; ✗ Not to know — an infinitive cannot open a reason clause; ✗ Not having known — the perfect form says the ignorance ended before they moved the samples, but they still didn't know.

items.q: Instead of ______ any one player ______ for blame, the coach said the whole squad had underperformed in the second half.
items.vi: Thay vì chỉ trích riêng một cầu thủ nào, huấn luyện viên nói rằng cả đội đã thi đấu dưới sức trong hiệp hai.
items.explanation: Double blank: Instead of is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing; the phrasal verb single somebody out = pick one person from a group for blame or praise. ✗ single / out — a bare verb cannot follow a preposition; ✗ singled / out — a past form cannot follow of; ✗ singling / up — single up does not exist.

items.q: With the two sides level after extra time, the semi-final will be decided by ______ keeps their nerve in the penalty shoot-out.
items.vi: Với hai đội hòa nhau sau hiệp phụ, trận bán kết sẽ được định đoạt bởi bất cứ ai giữ được bình tĩnh trong loạt sút luân lưu.
items.explanation: Pronoun: the blank is the subject of keeps and means 'the person who', so whoever; by governs the whole clause whoever keeps their nerve, not the pronoun alone. ✗ whomever — object form, but the word is the subject of keeps; ✗ who — needs a noun before it (the side who…) and cannot mean 'anyone who' in standard usage; ✗ whom — object form, and also needs an antecedent.

items.q: For four decades he was a ______ figure in sports broadcasting, whose commentary shaped how a whole generation heard the game.
items.vi: Trong bốn thập kỷ, ông là một tượng đài của ngành bình luận thể thao, người mà lời bình đã định hình cách cả một thế hệ nghe trận đấu.
items.explanation: Word choice: a person of outstanding importance whose commentary shaped a whole generation is a towering figure (fixed pairing). ✗ lofty — high-minded (lofty ideals) or arrogant (a lofty manner), not 'important'; ✗ soaring — rising fast, of prices, temperatures or birds; ✗ elevated — physically raised (an elevated railway) or high in rank, not said of a figure.

items.q: Unregulated betting apps ______ a serious threat to the integrity of lower-league football, the inquiry concluded.
items.vi: Các ứng dụng cá cược không được quản lý đặt ra mối đe dọa nghiêm trọng đối với sự trong sạch của bóng đá hạng dưới, cuộc điều tra kết luận.
items.explanation: Collocation: pose a threat to something is the fixed verb + noun for being a danger — apps pose a serious threat to the integrity. ✗ put — you put something at risk or under threat, never put a threat; ✗ make — make a threat = say threatening words, not be a danger; ✗ set — sets a record, a target or a trap, not a threat.

items.q: Nobody in the press room expected the manager to announce his resignation that afternoon, ______?
items.vi: Không ai trong phòng họp báo ngờ rằng huấn luyện viên sẽ tuyên bố từ chức chiều hôm đó, phải không?
items.explanation: Question tag: Nobody makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive; indefinite pronouns (nobody, everyone) take they, and past simple expected takes did: did they. ✗ didn't they — a negative tag after an already negative statement; ✗ didn't he — negative, and he points to the manager (the object), not the subject nobody; ✗ did he — right polarity, but he is the wrong pronoun for nobody.
